[...]
Panama are the clear outsiders in Group L, ranked well below England and Croatia. The expanded 48-team format, where the four best third-placed teams advance, offers a slim but real lifeline. Their realistic target is the match against Ghana on June 17 in Toronto — likely the game that defines whether they can compete for a knockout spot.
[...]
For Panama, simply being competitive and avoiding the winless, pointless return of 2018 would mark progress. A win — their first-ever at a World Cup — would be a historic achievement, and sneaking into the round of 32 would be a national triumph.
[...]
Under Thomas Christiansen, Panama are organised, disciplined and pragmatic. Expect a compact defensive block, deep lines against superior opponents, and a reliance on counter-attacks, set-pieces and the leadership of Godoy and Carrasquilla. Christiansen’s long tenure has instilled a clear identity and team cohesion that punches above the squad’s individual quality. The trade-off is limited creativity in sustained attack against deep blocks; Panama are at their best when defending a structure and breaking at speed.

Panama’s World Cup story is short but emotional. Their debut at Russia 2018 followed a famous qualifying campaign that ended in national celebration. The tournament itself was a brutal lesson at the elite level:
[...]
of their group
[...]
- Underdog romance — a small nation chasing its first-ever World Cup win and point.
- The England rematch — redemption beckons against the side that beat them 6–1 in 2018.
- Passionate support — “La Marea Roja” brings colour, noise and emotion to every match.
- Giant-killer potential — a well-drilled, experienced side that can frustrate the favourites.
[...]
Spirited group-stage campaign — a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic ambition, with knockout qualification a long shot.
[...]
Panama are the outsiders to qualify from Group L. Their season hinges on the opener against Ghana — a result there could keep alive hopes of a best-third-place finish in the expanded format. More likely, Panama will be competitive but fall short of the knockout rounds, with a maiden World Cup win or point representing genuine success. Projected: spirited group-stage campaign; a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic ambition, with knockout qualification a long shot.

results.title: Fifa World Cup 2026: What you need to know about South Korea - BBC Sport
highlights:
South Korea coach Hong Myung-Bo has been booed regularly during matches with fans unhappy at his conservative tactics
[...]
Despite going unbeaten in their 16 qualifiers, scoring 40 and conceding just eight, optimism is in short supply amongst Korean fans.
[...]
A lack of trust in the tactics of coach Hong Myung-Bo – who captained the Taegeuk Warriors to the 2002 semis - has led to a form of apathy.
[...]
Hong, who is regularly booed by fans, has tried to move away from their usual high pressing 4-2-3-1 to experiment with a safety-first, back three/five in recent fixtures. as he believes that a back four isnt enough defenders for a World Cup. Results, though, have been decidedly mixed with the new system proving to be far from watertight.
[...]
Heavy recent beatings (0-5 v Brazil, 0-4 v Ivory Coast) further eroded faith in Hong Myung-Bo.
[...]
Already South Korea's record caps holder, Son Heung-min is just two goals shy of Cha Bum-kun's all-time mark of 58. Without an MLS goal this season, he joked that he been saving them all for what is his fourth - and probably - final World Cup.
[...]
Hong Myung-Bo
[...]
They were unbeaten with a record of W11, D5 and conceded just eight goals. However, two draws with Palestine were heavily criticised.
[...]
When South Korea departed for their high-altitude training camp in Utah (they play all three group-stage matches in Mexico,
[...]
thin air of Guadalajara) there was none of the usual fanfare, nor for the first time since
[...]
a farewell send off game.
[...]
Hong Myung-Bo guided the Taeguk Warriors to an 11th consecutive World Cup as the only unbeaten Asian side in qualifying, but instead of that fuelling optimism a cloud of negativity has hung over their World Cup preperations.
[...]
The coach is a lightning rod for criticism and even his legendary playing career stopped offering him protection from the wrath of fans and media a long-time ago.
[...]
A controversial interview by his Portuguese assistant Joao Aroso, since deleted and blamed on poor translation, led to accusations that Hong is merely a 'puppet' and doesn't actually coach the team.
[...]
He can ill-afford to not add to their measly tally of just seven wins in 38 World Cup matches - three of which came in 2002 alone – especially as their draw looks so favourable.

Progressing out of Group A that contains Mexico (15th in world rankings), Czech Republic (41) & South Africa (60) is a basic requirement, but few have conviction that he's the man to carry them further.

results.title: From Dream to Expectation: Panama 2026 World Cup Preview
highlights:
From Dream to Expectation: Panama 2026 World Cup Preview
[...]
Panama did not sneak through or rely on a single famous night. Over the last few years, they have established themselves as one of CONCACAF's most consistent sides.
[...]
Under Thomas Christiansen, the national team has become one of the most competitive sides in CONCACAF, and while nobody is predicting a deep tournament run, there is genuine belief that the Red Tide can be more than just participants this summer.
[...]
After he was appointed in 2020, Panama was still searching for direction after the highs of the 2018 World Cup. The squad needed renewal, confidence and a clearer identity.
[...]
Panama had
[...]
. Christiansen did not abandon those qualities,
[...]
he added a
[...]
, encouraging his teams
[...]
For many supporters, he is already one of the most important figures in the country's football history.
[...]
If Panama were to challenge for a place in the knockout rounds, Carrasquilla would almost certainly be at the centre of that story.
[...]
That leaves Ghana and Panama battling for what could become a crucial third-place finish.
[...]
The opening match against Ghana already feels enormous.
[...]
A positive result would immediately put the Red Tide in contention for progression. A defeat would leave very little room for error heading into matches against stronger opposition.
[...]
With the expanded 48-team format allowing some third-place teams to advance, four points may be enough to keep qualification hopes alive for Panama.
[...]
It means Panama may not need to pull off a major upset to keep their tournament alive.
[...]
The expectations surrounding Panama today are very different from those that existed before Russia 2018. Back then, qualification itself was an achievement.
[...]
This time, there is ambition to do more.
[...]
Nobody expects the Red Tide to challenge for the trophy, but reaching the knockout stage feels like a realistic objective rather than a fantasy.
[...]
The expanded format gives them an opportunity, while the stability provided by Christiansen gives them belief.
[...]
There is also a growing confidence within Panamanian football itself.
[...]
Eight years ago, Panama arrived at their first World Cup simply hoping to enjoy the occasion. This time, they arrive believing they can compete.
[...]
Supporters flood stadiums dressed in red, creating the atmosphere that earned them the nickname "The Red Tide." The passion that greeted qualification in 2018 has not disappeared. If anything, it has grown stronger.
[...]
In 2018, every World Cup moment felt like a bonus. Eight years later, Panama arrive with higher expectations and a squad that expects to compete rather than simply participate.
